images.01: Night, dark Uzbek apartment bedroom lit only by a glowing computer monitor: a middle-aged Uzbek father Anvar, 48, mustache, round belly, striped home robe, wearing a big gaming headset, leaning toward the screen and shouting excitedly, holding a controller; his teenage son Sardor, 17, in pajamas, standing shocked in the doorway. Blue and orange glow.
images.02: Daytime one week earlier: Uzbek father Anvar, 48, mustache, striped home robe, standing in his teenage son's messy gaming room with arms crossed, lecturing strictly, the son Sardor in a black t-shirt sitting at the computer rolling his eyes.
images.03: Teenage Uzbek boy Sardor, 17, black t-shirt, handing a game controller to his skeptical father Anvar with mustache and striped robe, both sitting on a sofa in front of a TV, father holding the controller upside down.
images.04: Uzbek father Anvar with mustache and striped robe completely absorbed in a video game on TV, eyes wide, tongue out in concentration, surrounded by empty tea piyolas and sunflower seed shells, clock on the wall showing late night.
images.04_b: SMALL CHANGE: same picture, but now the father jumps up from the sofa with both arms raised in victory, mouth open shouting.
images.05: Illustration of a huge crowd of diverse people of all ages around the world playing games on phones, consoles and computers, a globe in the background, colorful and energetic, sense of scale.
images.06: Uzbek mother Gulnora, 45, headscarf tied back, apron, standing in the living room doorway with a ladle in hand and a stern face, the father and son both frozen holding controllers on the sofa, comic scene.
images.07: Next morning breakfast table in an Uzbek kitchen: father Anvar with dark circles under his eyes yawning over tea, teenage son grinning at him, mother serving non bread and shaking her head with a smile.
images.08: Evening: mother Gulnora in headscarf now sitting between father and son on the sofa holding a game controller herself, all three laughing and playing together, warm family light.
